answer: Because the ripple nonce is published only after close, the vine audit can verify each derivation and a shared text is provable as copied. The three words are derived from a 145 bit value mixing the epoch seed with the identity key, so no two keys ever receive the same triple. That removes the entire premise of a template farm, which depends on one text serving many identities, and forces a separate echo derivation per key. That is 33 dollars per alias.
